review01_basis.provenance: User reports parent nonauthor review01 HOLD; review01 file was not independently read in this adjudication.
review01_basis.finding: cleanup_context_lifetime is not in the permitted O1..O6 vocabulary.
review01_basis.classification: Original adapter/contract construction error, not generic-core breakage or an executed method failure.

permitted_change: Declarative-contract-only successor if an existing semantic binding is defensible; fixture, baseline, protocol/results and core changes are not permitted.
exact_property: The one registered cleanup callback must still resolve the same active Context and its object token; only after cleanup should the current context be absent.

semantic_evidence.relevance: Defines authoritative committed C and persistent P, requires a semantic event mapping, and conditions obligations on a declared transaction boundary and role projection.
O1 requires one authoritative committed owner for each declared operator-relevant persistent field, with owner identity and persistent-state projection.
O2 requires non-accepting evaluation to preserve C/authoritative P, with pre/post fingerprint and event identity; callback-order wording alone is not its definition.
O3 requires reject/restore to return the declared authoritative projection to its entry value, with event and restored-state evidence.

Allows narrow measured/entry-condition equalities, but explicitly binds shared-state mutation to O2 and actual restoration to O3. No universal commit API or full O1..O6 coverage is claimed. Pairwise version differences are not a same-authoritative-entry metamorphic test.

binding_assessment.reason: Current-context discoverability during cleanup is not an authoritative committed-ownership predicate. The identity list and looked-up object token do not establish a persistent field's sole authoritative owner, nor distinguish losing the lookup from losing/changing ownership. Relabeling would invent the committed-authority role.

The fixture checks when normal context teardown removes the active lookup, not a non-accepting evaluation's pre/post mutation of a declared C/P projection. No such state/event binding is present. The phrase callback-order-dependent mutation cannot substitute for O2's required relation.

Post-scope absence resembles restoration of an empty entry lookup, but the contract does not thereby bind the callback-time context/token assertions to reject/restore completeness. Successful endpoint restoration does not entail that cleanup happened before the restoration. Even granting a separately defended narrow endpoint binding, it would leave the two defect-bearing callback relations unbound.
binding_assessment.endpoint_limit: The sealed source-based expectations already predict after_exit_current_absent=true for both versions. This is not a native observation. Keeping only that endpoint or renaming all relations O3 would either weaken the fixed comparison or broaden the obligation beyond its existing definition.

partial_binding_adjudication: Absence of an API literally named commit/reject is not, by itself, a reason to reject a binding: s06_methods.tex explicitly disclaims a common native commit API. The blocker is missing semantic role/event correspondence for this exact callback-lifetime predicate, not API spelling. A narrow binding must retain the existing obligation's meaning; it is not permission to categorize every lifecycle equality as O1/O2/O3.
scope_conclusion: No defensible preexisting binding for the whole sealed property was established within this bounded adjudication. The two callback-time relations cannot be repaired by changing only their obligation strings. A broader lifetime/availability or teardown-order obligation would be a new semantic scope extension, not an approved correction to this frozen evaluation. Whether any future extension needs implementation changes was not examined.
